title: Volume Concession on Priced Blocks of Included Miles for a Keyturn Trip Booking
content:
A concession comes off each priced block of included miles on a Keyturn Trip Booking where the top-up is a large one and the trip has already been running for some time.

1. Where the top-up added 4000 miles or more and the trip has run for at least 28 days, that is four weeks, the volume concession is 15.00 USD off each priced block.
2. Where the top-up added 2000 miles or more but fewer than 4000 and the trip has run for at least 28 days, the volume concession is 8.00 USD off each priced block.
3. In every other case no volume concession is given.

The days the trip has run are counted from the day the trip actually started to the day of handling, the day it started not counted and the day of handling counted.

### The two conditions together

| Miles the top-up added | Days the trip has run | Volume concession for each priced block |
|---|---|---|
| 4000 or more | 28 or more | 15.00 USD |
| 2000 or more but fewer than 4000 | 28 or more | 8.00 USD |
| Fewer than 2000 | 28 or more | None |
| Any | Fewer than 28 | None |

The mile figures are reached rather than passed: a top-up of exactly 4000 miles takes 15.00 USD, and one of exactly 2000 miles takes 8.00 USD. A top-up of 3999 miles falls into the second band, not the first. Twenty-eight days is likewise reached rather than passed.

Both limbs must hold. A top-up of 5000 miles on a trip that has been running 19 days attracts no concession at all, because the second limb fails.

*Hypothetical.* On a trip that has been running 33 days, a top-up adding 4200 miles carries a concession of 15.00 USD off each priced block; a top-up adding 2600 miles carries 8.00 USD off each priced block; and a top-up adding 900 miles carries none.
